name: Jordan

latest_census.notes: General Population and Housing Census of 30 November 2015 (previous: 2004, 1994); the next was planned for around 2025 and I cannot confirm its status. Ethnicity: not asked. What the 2015 census asked and published prominently is nationality (Jordanian, Syrian, Egyptian, Palestinian, Iraqi, Yemeni, Libyan, other) -- the packet's 'ethnicity' shares (Jordanian 69.3, Syrian 13.3, Palestinian 6.7, Egyptian 6.7) are that citizenship table, which this repo's rules refuse as ethnicity (the Nigeria/Sudan/Libya precedent in docs/SOURCES.md). Religion: I cannot say with confidence whether the 2015 questionnaire carried a religion item; the Factbook's shares (Muslim 97.1, Christian 2.1, Buddhist 0.4, Hindu 0.1) look like a full-resident count that includes migrant workers, which would point to the 2015 census, but I have not seen a DoS religion table -- leave null and have the runner look for one. Language: not asked.

subnational_sources.title: 2015 General Population and Housing Census -- main results tables: population by nationality, sex, governorate and district (NATIONALITY = citizenship, refused as ethnicity by repo convention)
subnational_sources.matches_boundary_level: admin1 (12 governorates = 12); districts approximately admin2 (52 shapes)
subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled: DoS released the 2015 census results as Excel/PDF tables on dosweb.dos.gov.jo organised by governorate and district, and the nationality-by-governorate table was widely quoted (Amman, Irbid, Mafraq and Zarqa carrying most Syrians). Listed so the owner can see what exists; it is a citizenship count, not an ethnicity count.

subnational_sources.evidence: Not recalled with confidence; entered only as the thing the runner should look for in the same results workbook. If absent, religion is unknown-not-asked (D), not a not_collected declaration.

subnational_sources.evidence: Recalled with low confidence that Jordan 2004 is in IPUMS with nationality and possibly religion variables; verify.

tier_reason: DoS publishes the 2015 census by governorate (12 = admin1) and district in XLSX/PDF, but the field it certainly carries is nationality, which the repo refuses as ethnicity, and whether a religion table exists is unconfirmed; language and ethnicity proper are not asked.
recommended_action: Crawl dosweb.dos.gov.jo for the 2015 census results workbooks (Arabic and English editions). If a religion-by-governorate table is present, build admin1 (12 governorates: Ajloun, Amman, Aqaba, Balqa, Irbid, Jerash, Karak, Ma'an, Madaba, Mafraq, Tafilah, Zarqa) and try the district table for admin2 (the boundary file's 52 shapes mix governorate and district names -- 'Amman', 'Al-Balqa', 'Az-Zarqa' -- so expect a partial join). Declare language not_collected. Do not load the nationality table as ethnicity; if the owner wants it, label it citizenship.

summary: Jordan's DoS (dosweb.dos.gov.jo) ran its last census in November 2015 and publishes its tables by governorate (12 = admin1) and district in Excel and PDF. The certain subnational field is nationality (Jordanian/Syrian/Egyptian/Palestinian...), which is citizenship and is refused as ethnicity under the repo's own rule; ethnicity proper and language are not asked. Whether a religion table exists is the open question -- the Factbook's shares including Buddhist and Hindu residents hint at a 2015 count, but I cannot confirm one, so Tier B pending the runner's look at the 2015 workbooks.
